newsitem.title: KENYA: Financials boost Nairobi bourse index.
newsitem.headline: Financials boost Nairobi bourse index.

text.p: A rise in demand for financials pushed the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) 20-share index up 8.32 points to stand at 3124.14 on Friday, brokers said.
Brokers and bourse officials said the increase in demand was due to good results expected sometime in February.
Turnover dropped to 6.392 million shillings traded on 159,964 shares from 14.799 million shillings traded on 267,201 shares.
"The market was not very active today. Most activity revolved around the financials," a bourse official said.
Barclays closed at 101 from 100, while Kenya Commercial Bank gained 1.50 to close at 74. Standard Chartered Bank traded at 49 from 48.25 while Housing Finance Company closed at 19 from 18.60.
A broker said speculation centered around the four major listed institutions -- Kenya Commercial, Standard, Barclays, and Housing Finance Co.
"We really do not expect them to post superprofits," he said. "But what will be interesting to watch are those companies which converted from financial institutions to banks."
"Barclays is normally the first to announce and this might trigger off buying interest in the others," another added.
National Industrial Credit traded at 41 unchanged, while Diamond Trust Bank eased to 31.50 from 32.
Prices on other shares remained stable with very little trading activity going on.
Power distribution monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting eased to 140 from 141, while oil concern Total Kenya gained 2.0 to close at 67.
